specification.title: A managed transaction requests SERIALIZABLE
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's managed transaction API, the one that runs a callback inside the transaction and commits when it returns, requesting the isolation level in settings.isolation_level (SERIALIZABLE). The server's default is READ COMMITTED. If the API raises instead of starting the transaction, record its error and go to step 6.
Write the marker `tx` through the framework's ordinary write API, and make sure that write was sent.

Read the marker back through the framework's ordinary query API, inside the same transaction, and make sure the read reached PostgreSQL: a query, not a lookup in the framework's identity map or cache. The runner confirms it by the transaction's AccessShareLock on item.
Checkpoint `after-read`: in one statement, through the transaction's own connection, read pg_current_xact_id(), pg_backend_pid() and current_setting('transaction_isolation'), and report all three.
Return from the callback normally, so that the framework commits the transaction. Then go to the last step.

Only if the API raised at step 1: start a plain transaction through the same managed API, with no isolation level. Inside it, at checkpoint `baseline`, report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(), then end it normally. If the plain transaction fails too, report its error in steps.baseline. Report the outcome failed, with step 1's error as api_error.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned (after step 6, when it ran): the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: On PostgreSQL, a transaction that the API started at a requested isolation level runs at that level or a stricter one, never at a weaker one.
An API whose documentation accepts an isolation level that PostgreSQL supports does not reject a valid request for that level: it starts the transaction.

execution.description: Database.BeginTransactionAsync, CommitAsync, and RollbackAsync. Marker inserts use Database.ExecuteSqlAsync. The native TX-01A violation is SaveChangesAsync, which EF Core wraps in a savepoint. Nested scopes use CreateSavepointAsync. Pooling is false. EnableRetryOnFailure is not called. The provider's default execution strategy is left in place.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: A successful start does not tell the application which level PostgreSQL applied; only current_setting('transaction_isolation'), read inside the transaction, does. An application that requested SERIALIZABLE and got no error relies on its guarantee: concurrent transactions behave as if they had run one at a time. A rejected request reaches the application as an error, so it can decide what to do instead.

evaluation.reason: EF Core has no managed transaction API that runs a callback and commits when the callback returns, and that accepts an isolation level. ExecutionStrategy.ExecuteAsync is a retry policy. AutoTransactionBehavior starts an implicit transaction around SaveChanges and does not take an isolation level. BeginTransactionAsync is the explicit API and is the other case.

reproduction.requires: pnpm run setup, then pnpm run pg:up (README.md)
